what_this_is: The acceptance matrix for POST /sessions/report, POST /sessions/timeline and
READ-ONLY source snapshot of the backend, plus the payloads this plugin actually serializes today.
The `report` and `timeline` sections are pinned to the `provenance.backend_commit` snapshot below.
The `me/cli-agent/account` section carries its OWN provenance block, because it was transcribed
from a LATER tree and part of it describes a target the backend has not merged yet — read it there.
A source snapshot is evidence of a SCHEMA. It is not evidence of what any environment deploys, and
nothing in `gates` below is closed by reading a file — every one of them needs a live check.
The payloads under `payloads` are generated, never hand-written: run the contract test with
BEEZI_CONTRACT_FIXTURE_WRITE=1 to re-serialize them through lib/checkpoint.mjs.

account_uuid.note: 255 is the §4 E5 TARGET and is in no commit; SessionReportRequestDto still says @MaxLength(64). E5 raises the bound on BOTH DTOs, so this rule and me/cli-agent/account's accountUuid move together — recording only one of them would make the report route look narrower than the check-in route for the same id. Ids are never truncated to fit, because a truncated id is a wrong id and mints a phantom subscription row. Until E5 DEPLOYS, lib/checkpoint.mjs also does not EMIT an id longer than deployed_maxLength: a @MaxLength violation fails the global ValidationPipe, which rejects the whole session report rather than the one field, so an SSO seat would lose all of its analytics instead of just its account column. It omits the id and falls through to email-anchored resolution. Retire that cap (WIRE_ACCOUNT_ID_MAX in lib/checkpoint.mjs) when deployed_maxLength here reads 255.

me/cli-agent/account.unknown_property_behavior: 400 BadRequest for the whole check-in (global pipe: whitelist + forbidNonWhitelisted). This is why a key-name drift is a silent total failure rather than a dropped field.

accountUuid.note: 255 is the §4 E5 TARGET and is in no commit; the tree still enforces 64. Ids are sent verbatim — never truncated to fit, because a truncated id is a wrong id and mints a phantom subscription row.

subscriptionType.note: Lenient bounded string, normalized server-side. Carries the RAW plan text for the server's alias-discovery loop.

rateLimitTier.note: Declared by the DTO; Cursor has no equivalent, so this client omits it.

subscriptionStatus.note: §4 E3 TARGET, present in NO commit. Emitting it against an undeployed tenant 400s the entire check-in under forbidNonWhitelisted.

keys.note: Declared by the DTO; API-key fingerprinting is a Claude Code mechanism with no Cursor equivalent, so this client omits it.

prefix.note: DELIBERATELY no notEmpty. `prefix` is @IsString @MaxLength(32) with no minimum, so '' passes server-side; `last4` is @Length(1, 8), which is why only IT carries notEmpty. Do not 'fix' this into symmetry — the asymmetry is the DTO.

credential.unknown_property_behavior: 400 — @ValidateNested with the global whitelist applies forbidNonWhitelisted to the nested objects too
credential.validator_note: `length`'s `max: 8192` is recorded from @Max(8192) but is NOT enforced by this fixture's validator: checkValue's `int` branch understands `min` only. Do not read a green run as proof an over-long length would be accepted.
credential.service_clamp: prefix and last4 are bounded generously here (32 / 8) and clamped hard by the service to 12 / 4 — validation states the wire contract, the service enforces the privacy rule, and neither trusts the other.

me/cli-agent/account.client_position: Nothing is sent yet. lib/account-sync.mjs still has ACCOUNT_CHECKIN_ENDPOINT = null, deps.enabled defaulting false, zero production callers, and a CHECKIN_PAYLOAD_FIELDS allowlist whose every name (environment, cursorAccountEmail, cursorAccountSource, plan, planSource, planObservedAt, billingSource) is outside accepted_properties above — today's payload would 400 in full. Plan §4 B2 rewrites it to the camelCase names above and owns the subset assertion against this section. `rateLimitTier` and `keys` stay omitted (Cursor has neither); `subscriptionStatus` is read locally by §4 A1 but stays OFF the wire until E3's migration and code release are verified per tenant — §6 puts step 2 (E3/E5) before step 4 (B2) for exactly that reason, and §5 records new-client/old-server as the unsafe direction.

gates.status: OPEN — blocks every Cursor report at this snapshot
gates.what: This plugin emits `models` as an ARRAY of (model, billing_pool) rows. The snapshot's DTO requires `Record<string, ICliAgentModelUsage>` and its validator rejects arrays outright, so every Cursor report would 400 and lose that segment's tokens, cost, code changes and operations together.
gates.why_the_array_exists: Cursor is the only agent whose ONE model in ONE segment can legitimately have two rows — the seat-covered part and the credits-paid part. A record keyed by model cannot hold both, and flattening to a model-only record would silently drop one billing pool.
gates.closing_evidence: A deployed backend that accepts a Cursor (model, billing_pool) shape — either a keyed record whose key carries the pool, or an array accepted alongside the existing record for old clients — demonstrated against the target environment with a real authenticated report.

gates.what: CORRECTED. This entry used to claim that resolveBeeziAgent knows claude-code and codex only and that `cursor` therefore resolves to claude-code. That was true at the pinned snapshot 871a788 and is FALSE at the portal working tree 62610eb: `BeeziAgent.CURSOR = 'cursor'` exists, AGENT_BY_HEADER_VALUE maps the header value `cursor` to it, and machineToolFor/analyticsSourceFor carry it to LinkedMachineTool.CURSOR and AnalyticsSource.CURSOR. Only an ABSENT X-Beezi-Agent falls back to claude-code silently; a present-but-unrecognised value falls back with an `auth.beezi-agent.header.unrecognised` warn. `cursor` is recognised and is neither case. What remains OPEN is purely deployment: that tree is uncommitted/undeployed (see docs/gate-record.md), so no environment is proven to answer this way yet, and against an OLD deployment Cursor usage would still land as Claude Code.
gates.closing_evidence: A live authenticated request carrying `X-Beezi-Agent: cursor` against the target environment, shown to be stored with a cursor source/tool — plus the identity routes this plugin calls (/me/cursor/...). Source proof at 62610eb is not deployment proof.

gates.what: `state` is a bounded string (<=50) and `break` is already a member of CliAgentActivityState at this commit, excluded from activity-breakdown totals. So the schema accepts it; whether the DEPLOYED reader knows it is unverified.
gates.client_position: The client keeps `break` behind options.allowBreakState, default OFF. Nothing emits it today.

gates.what: `waiting_subtype` is an optional bounded string and `command_approval` is a known member. The Cursor client can only emit it from a caller-validated permission marker, and nothing on this host produces one yet.
gates.closing_evidence: A Cursor host signal that identifies a permission/approval wait, captured from a real install.

gates.what: The fields this lane derives already exist in the snapshot DTO: `claude_md_lines` + `project_instructions_status` for the rules reader, `context_peak_tokens` / `context_final_tokens` / `context_final_model` for the context metrics, and `models[].by_effort` for the effort buckets. gates.closing_evidence: Backend owner agreement on the Cursor meaning of `claude_md_lines`, a deployed route that stores the context fields for a Cursor source, and a DTO revision adding a host-version property if one is wanted.
